Separation of responsibilities

The frontend owns presentation, routing, form feedback, and local filtering. The backend owns authentication, validation, scheduling rules, database access, and consistent responses. PostgreSQL owns persistence, foreign keys, and transaction locking. Mock records are database seeds; they never replace real CRUD calls.

frontend/  src/pages, src/components, auth, api, hooks, styles
backend/   src/routes in app.js, services, validation, auth, db
           db/SQL migration and seed; test/API integration tests
tests/     Playwright user workflows
docs/      Screenshots, submission links, PDF, Loom checklist
render.yaml  Separate Render services + managed PostgreSQL

Authentication and errors

The seeded staff password is bcrypt-hashed. Eight-hour JWTs protect clinic routes and are kept in browser session storage. Logout clears the token; expired sessions return to login. Login attempts are rate limited. Validation errors include field messages; unexpected server errors use a generic response and server-side logging.

Concurrency decision

Appointment writes lock the selected doctor row inside a database transaction, then check for overlapping non-cancelled visits. Concurrent requests for the same doctor wait and recheck after the first commit. Adjacent visits remain valid. Foreign keys prevent orphan appointments.

Database model and API

TableFields / relationship
staffid, unique email, password_hash
doctorsid, name, specialization, phone, email, availability JSONB, active, created_at
appointmentsid, patient_name, patient_contact, doctor_id → doctors.id, starts_at, ends_at, reason, status, created_at

Relationship: One doctor has many appointments. Doctor deletion is restricted while referenced; staff can deactivate the doctor. Availability has ISO weekday keys and local start/end intervals. PostgreSQL timestamps represent UTC instants; UI display and date filters use Asia/Karachi by default.

MethodRoutePurpose
GET/api/healthPublic database readiness
POST / GET/api/auth/login · /api/auth/meLogin / session check
GET/api/dashboardCounts and upcoming visits
GET / POST/api/doctorsList/search / create
GET / PATCH / DELETE/api/doctors/:idDetail / edit / delete
GET / POST/api/appointmentsList/filter / create
GET / PATCH / DELETE/api/appointments/:idDetail / edit / delete

Appointment filters: date, doctor_id, status, and patient search. Statuses: pending, confirmed, completed, cancelled. Required fields are validated in both UI and API. Durations default to 30 minutes, must be positive and at most eight hours, and must fit the active doctor's availability when scheduling. Cancelled visits release their slot.

Success: { "success": true, "data": ... }
Error:   { "success": false, "message": "...", "fields": { ... } }
HTTP: 200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 409, 429, 500, 503

Local setup and deployment

Install Node.js 24, npm, and PostgreSQL 14+. Copy each application's .env.example, configure credentials, and create clinic and clinic_test databases.

npm ci
npm ci --prefix backend
npm ci --prefix frontend
npm run db:migrate --prefix backend
npm run db:seed --prefix backend
npm run dev

Frontend: http://localhost:5173. API: http://localhost:4000/api. Sign in with the configured STAFF_EMAIL and STAFF_PASSWORD. Use independent dev commands inside either application when needed.

Backend environmentFrontend environment
DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, FRONTEND_URL, STAFF_EMAIL, STAFF_PASSWORD, PORT, CLINIC_TIMEZONE, TEST_DATABASE_URLVITE_API_URL (public API URL ending in /api)

Render

Push develop to GitHub, connect a Render Blueprint using render.yaml, and supply environment values. Backend root: backend; build: npm ci; start: npm run start:render; health: /api/health. Frontend root: frontend; build: npm ci && npm run build; publish: dist; rewrite /* to /index.html. Managed PostgreSQL is connected through DATABASE_URL. Verify assigned origins and redeploy after environment changes. No GitHub Actions are needed.

Checks and limitations

npm run lint
npm test
npm run build
npm run test:e2e

Backend coverage: authentication, JWT expiry, request validation, doctor/appointment CRUD, joins and filters, inactive doctors, availability boundaries, overlapping and concurrent requests, reference protection, seed preservation, and dashboard counts. Browser coverage: protected navigation, all CRUD actions, persistence after refresh, conflict feedback, confirmation cancellation, mobile layout, keyboard dismissal, error recovery, and expired sessions. Screenshots on the following pages are captured from the running local application.

One staff role; no password reset, account administration, billing, reminders, pagination, holiday exceptions, or audit log. Existing visits are not moved when availability changes. Public deployment checks, the candidate's Loom recording, and Drive sharing remain pending until real account URLs are recorded. Free Render services have cold starts; free PostgreSQL expires after 30 days. See Render resource limitations.
